To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BH3‐only proteins Bim and BMF are essential regulators of haematopoiesis and HSPC survival and transplantation efficacy, and that RNAi‐mediated depletion of BIM and BMF, or RNAi‐mediation‐based BCL‐2‐overexpression, may be a promising strategy to enhance HSPC survival.
the BH3‐only proteins Bim and/or Bmf are essential for the regulation of HSPC survival, and that their depletion or inhibition by BCL‐2 overexpression can improve HSPC engraftment.

the pro‐apoptosis proteins Bim and BMF, but not other BH3‐only proteins, critically contribute to the regulation of HSPC survival during early engrafts, while BIM, but not BMF, is essential for long‐term HSPC survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of apoptosis in haematopoietically active cells, and the role of apoptosis in the regulation of haemopoiesis.
the identification of novel molecular targets for stem cell‐based therapies and the elucidation of their mechanisms of action.
the identification and characterization of novel targets for the treatment of haematological malignancies and other disorders that are associated with a loss of HSPC function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bim and Bcl‐2, but not Bmf, are the most relevant regulators of HSPCs in culture and in vivo.
Bim and Bfm are critical regulators of HSPCs survival and that their modulation might be a useful strategy to improve stem cell transplantation efficacy.
the pro‐apoptosis BH3‐only proteins Bim and BMF are key regulators of HSPCs survival and transplantation efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the balance of pro‐ and anti‐apoptotic members of the Bcl‐2 protein family is critical to maintain the homeostasis of HSPCs.
the balance between pro‐apoptosis (Bim and Bmf) and anti‐apoptosis proteins (Bcl‐2) in haematopoietal stem cells (HSPCs) is critical for HSPC survival, transplantation and reconstitution.
the balance of pro‐survival versus pro‐apoptosis signalling is crucially regulated by Bcl‐2 proteins in haematopoietetic stem cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Bcl‐2 proteins are critical regulators of haematopoiesis and that targeting of Bcl‐independent pathways, i.e. the BH3‐only proteins Bim and/or Bmf, may be a promising strategy to improve haematopoietietic stem cell transplantation.
Bim and Bfm are essential regulators of HSPCs dynamics in culture as well as after transplantation.
Bim and Bcl‐2, but not Bmf or Bcl‐xL, are important regulators of HSC fate after transplantation.
